'''KeePass Password Safe''' is a [[free and open-source]] [[password manager]] primarily for [[Windows]]. It officially supports [[macOS]] and [[Linux]] [[operating system]]s through the use of [[Mono (software)|Mono]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Setup |url=http://keepass.info/help/v2/setup.html#mono |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209093825/https://keepass.info/help/v2/setup.html#mono |archive-date=2023-12-09 |website=KeePass}}</ref> Additionally, there are several unofficial [[Porting|ports]] for [[Windows Phone]], [[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], and [[BlackBerry]] devices, which normally work with the same copied or shared (remote) password [[database]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Download |url=http://keepass.info/download.html |website=KeePass |access-date=2015-12-24 |archive-date=2021-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210722214225/https://keepass.info/download.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=7Pass |url=https://7pass.wordpress.com/ |via=Word press |access-date=2015-12-24 |archive-date=2020-05-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200505091627/https://7pass.wordpress.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=KeePassDroid |url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.android.keepass |website=Google Play Store |publisher=Brian Pellin |access-date=24 March 2024 |archive-date=2 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702083052/https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.android.keepass |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=BlackBerry World – KeePass for BlackBerry |url=http://appworld.blackberry.com/webstore/content/27406106/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130622164015/http://appworld.blackberry.com/webstore/content/27406106/ |archive-date=2013-06-22 |access-date=2014-03-26 |website=Appworld |publisher=Blackberry}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=iOS application |url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/minikeepass-secure-password/id451661808 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111010093932/http://itunes.apple.com/us/app/minikeepass-secure-password/id451661808 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 10, 2011 |website=[[iTunes]] |publisher=Apple}}</ref>  KeePass stores usernames, passwords, and other fields, including free-form notes and file attachments, in an encrypted [[Computer file|file]]. This file can be protected by any combination of a [[master password]], a key file, and the current Windows account details. By default, the KeePass database is stored on a local [[file system]] (as opposed to [[cloud storage]]).<ref name="Zukerman-5tools">{{Cite magazine |last=Zukerman |first=Erez |title=Tools for the Paranoid: 5 Free Security Tools to Protect Your Data |url=http://www.pcworld.com/article/2026561/tools-for-the-paranoid-5-free-security-tools-to-protect-your-data.html |access-date=2013-07-14 |magazine=[[PC World]]}}</ref>

KeePass comes in two different variants: KeePass 1.x and KeePass 2.x. Although the 1.x variant is the former variant it is supported indefinitely: Dominik Reichl: "2.x isn't the successor of 1.x, and 1.x isn't dead".<ref>{{Citation |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Development Status FAQ |work=KeePass |url=https://keepass.info/devstatus.html |access-date=2023-02-28 |archive-date=2023-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228142323/https://keepass.info/devstatus.html |url-status=live }}.</ref> KeePass 2.x has a different software basis in [[C Sharp (programming language)|C#]] instead of the former [[C++]]. Mainly [[Data communication |communication]] features are extended in KeePass 2.x: authentication with the [[Windows]] [[user account]], [[Remote access service|remote]] and shared database editing as well as many plugins allowing communication and authentication with different [[web browser]]s, [[database]]s and more.<ref>{{Citation |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Edition Comparison |work=KeePass |url=https://keepass.info/compare.html |access-date=2023-02-28 |archive-date=2023-02-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228142322/https://keepass.info/compare.html |url-status=live }}.</ref><ref name="auto" />

KeePass 1.x and 2.x support a number of [[Plug-in (computing)|plugins]], although 2.x allows more plugins.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Plugins |url=https://keepass.info/plugins.html |website=Keepass |access-date=2021-10-04 |archive-date=2021-02-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206130813/https://keepass.info/plugins.html |url-status=live }}</ref> It has a [[Random password generator|password generator]] and synchronization function, supports [[two-factor authentication]], and has a ''Secure Desktop'' mode. It can use a two-channel auto-type obfuscation feature to offer additional protection against [[Keystroke logging|keyloggers]].<ref name="Rubenking-Review">{{Cite magazine |last=Rubenking |first=Neil |title=KeePass Review & Ratings |url=https://www.pcmag.com/article2/0,2817,2408063,00.asp |access-date=2014-06-11 |magazine=[[PC Magazine]]}}</ref> KeePass can import from over 30 other most commonly used password managers.<ref name="Rubenking-Review" />

A 2017 [[Consumer Reports]] article described KeePass as one of the four most widely used password managers (alongside [[1Password]], [[Dashlane]] and [[LastPass]]), being "popular among tech enthusiasts" and offering the same level of security as non-free competitors.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chaikivsky |first=Andrew |date=2017-02-17 |title=Everything You Need to Know About Password Managers |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/digital-security/everything-you-need-to-know-about-password-managers/ |access-date=2018-06-23 |work=Consumer Reports |archive-date=2017-02-08 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20170208015826/http://www.consumerreports.org/digital-security/everything-you-need-to-know-about-password-managers/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

A 2019 Independent Security Evaluators study described KeePass as well as other widely used password managers as being unable to control [[Windows 10]]'s tendency to leave passwords in cleartext in RAM after they are displayed using Windows controlled GUI.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bednarek |first=Adrian |title=Password Managers: Under the Hood of Secrets Management |url=https://www.securityevaluators.com/casestudies/password-manager-hacking/ |access-date=2019-03-24 |website=Security evaluators}}</ref> In addition, several GitHub projects (KeeFarce, KeeThief, Lazanga) specifically attack a running KeePass to steal all data when the host is compromised. KeePass cannot prevent password theft and, as Dominik Reichl, the administrator of KeePass, states, "neither KeePass nor any other password manager can magically run securely in a spyware-infected, insecure environment."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Security Issues |url=https://keepass.info/help/kb/sec_issues.html#keefarce |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903210519/https://keepass.info/help/kb/sec_issues.html#keefarce |archive-date=2019-09-03 |access-date=2019-03-24 |website=KeePass}}</ref>

==Overview==

===Import and export===
The password list is saved by default as a <code>.kdbx</code> file, but it can be exported to [[.txt]], [[HTML]], [[Extensible Markup Language|XML]] and [[Comma-separated values|CSV]].<ref name="keefeat">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |date=2019 |title=Features |url=https://keepass.info/features.html |access-date=2019-12-31 |website=KeePass}}</ref> The XML output can be used in other applications and re-imported into KeePass using a plugin. The CSV output is compatible with many other password safes like the commercial closed-source Password Keeper and the closed-source Password Agent. Also, the CSVs can be imported by spreadsheet applications like Microsoft Excel or [[OpenOffice.org Calc |OpenOffice]]/[[LibreOffice Calc]].

KeePass 2.x has import support for several popular formats built-in. File format support can be expanded through the use of KeePass plugins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2.x Plugins |url=https://keepass.info/help/v2/plugins.html |access-date=2019-01-26 |website=KeePass}}</ref>

===Multi-user support===
KeePass supports simultaneous access and simultaneous changes to a shared password file by multiple computers (often by using a shared network drive), however there is no provisioning of access per-group or per-entry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=KeePass Help Center |url=http://keepass.info/help/base/multiuser.html |access-date=2012-12-28 |archive-date=2012-12-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121228164033/http://keepass.info/help/base/multiuser.html |url-status=live }}</ref> As of May 2014, there are no plugins available to add provisioned multi-user support, but there exists a [[proprietary software|proprietary]] password server (now titled Keepass Hub, formerly known as [[Pleasant Password Server]]) that is compatible with the KeePass client and includes provisioning.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Keepass Hub |url=https://keepasshub.com/details/features |access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref>

===Auto-type and drag and drop===
[[File:Keepass-autotype.gif|thumb|An example of KeePass's auto-type function, which is triggered by a global hotkey]]

KeePass can minimize itself and type the information of the currently selected entry into dialogs, webforms, etc. KeePass has a global auto-type hot key. When KeePass is running in the background (with an unlocked database) and user presses down the hotkey, it looks up the selected (or correct) entry and enters every login and/or password characters sequence.<ref name="CNET-Review">{{Cite web |last=Markton |first=Ben |title=KeePass Password Safe Professional |url=http://download.cnet.com/KeePass-Password-Safe-Professional/3000-2092_4-10916116.html |access-date=2014-06-11 |website=CNET |archive-date=2014-07-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714160937/http://download.cnet.com/KeePass-Password-Safe-Professional/3000-2092_4-10916116.html |url-status=live }}</ref> All fields, such as title, username, password, URL, and notes, can be [[drag and drop]]ped into other windows.{{citation needed|date=December 2018}}

Windows [[Clipboard (software)|clipboard]] handling allows double-clicking on any field of the password list to copy its value to the Windows clipboard. 

KeePass may be configured to randomize characters' input sequence to make it harder to [[Keystroke logging|log keystrokes]]. The features is called Two-Channel Auto-Type Obfuscation (TCATO).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Two-Channel Auto-Type Obfuscation |url=https://keepass.info/help/v2/autotype_obfuscation.html |access-date=2021-09-15 |website=Keepass}}</ref>

=== Clipboard reset ===
KeePass automatically clears the clipboard some time after the user has copied one of their passwords into it. KeePass features protection against clipboard monitors (other applications will not get notifications that the clipboard content has been changed).{{citation needed|date=December 2018}}

KeePass at one time had a paste-once functionality, where after a single paste operation, the clipboard would be cleared automatically, but this was removed in version 2.x due to incompatibility and insufficient effectiveness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=What happened to the paste-once functionality in 2.x? |url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/keepass/forums/forum/329220/topic/4925103 |access-date=2012-10-14 |website=KeePass Forums |via=Source forge}}</ref>

===Browser support===
The auto-type functionality works with all windows, and consequently with all browsers. The KeeForm extension fills in user details into website form fields automatically. It is available for [[Mozilla Firefox]], Google Chrome, and Microsoft Edge. Internet Explorer also has a browser integration [[toolbar]] available.<ref>{{Citation |title=KeeForm |url=http://www.keeform.org/ |accessdate=2014-06-24 |archive-date=2014-07-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712154453/http://keeform.org/ |url-status=live }}.</ref>

===Built-in password generator===
[[File:KeePass random password.png|thumb|User Interface of the password generator]]
KeePass features a built-in [[Random password generator|password generator]] that generates random passwords. Random seeding can be done through user input (mouse movement and random keyboard input).<ref name="CNET-Review" />

===Plugins===
KeePass has a plugin architecture. There are various plugins available from the KeePass website (such as import/export from/to various other formats, database backup, integration, automation, etc.). Note that plugins may compromise the security of KeePass, because they are written by independent authors and have full access to the KeePass database.<ref name="auto" />

===Wrapper===
KeePass has an opensource wrapper, QuicKeepass, that allows the use of KeePass more efficiently on Linux.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 28, 2021 |title=QuicKeepass |url=https://github.com/nongiach/QuicKeepass |via=GitHub}}</ref>

==Cryptography==

===Runtime security===
[[File:KeePass add entry.png|thumb|"Add Entry" dialog in KeePass]]

According to the utility's author, KeePass was one of the first password management utilities to use security-enhanced password edit controls, in this case one called CSecureEditEx.<ref name="keepass_secedit">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Secure Edit Controls |url=http://www.keepass.info/help/base/secedits.html |access-date=2009-11-14 |website=KeePass |archive-date=2010-01-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100126014052/http://keepass.info/help/base/secedits.html |url-status=live }}</ref>  The author makes several claims regarding the security of the control and its resistance to password revealing utilities; however, the author does not cite or make any references to any third-party testing of the control to corroborate the claims of its security.<ref name="secure_edit">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |date=2005-04-17 |title=CSecureEditEx – A More Secure Edit Control |url=http://www.codeproject.com/editctrl/SecEditEx.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060217114706/http://www.codeproject.com/editctrl/SecEditEx.asp |archive-date=2006-02-17 |website=The Code Project}}</ref>

Passwords are protected in memory while KeePass is running. On Windows Vista and later versions, passwords are encrypted in process memory using Windows [[Data Protection API]], which allows storing the key for memory protection in a secure, non-swappable memory area. On previous Windows systems, KeePass falls back to using the [[ARC4]] cipher with a temporary, random session key.<ref name="keepass_security">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Security |url=http://keepass.info/help/base/security.html |access-date=2007-12-13 |website=KeePass}}</ref>

===Offline security===
[[File:KeePass master key.png|thumb|Create master key]]
Access to the database is restricted by a master password or a key file. Both methods may be combined to create a "composite master key". If both methods are used, then both must be present to access the password database. KeePass version 2.x introduces a third option—dependency upon the current Windows user.<ref name="keepass2">{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Composite Master Key |url=http://keepass.info/help/base/keys.html |access-date=2009-11-14 |website=KeePass}}</ref>
KeePass encrypts the database with the [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]], [[Twofish]] or [[ChaCha20]] symmetric cipher, where the first two are used in CBC/PKCS7 mode. AES is the default option in both KeePass editions, Twofish is available in KeePass 1.x, ChaCha20 is available only in KeePass 2.35 and higher.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=News: KeePass 2.35 available! |url=https://keepass.info/news/n170109_2.35.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314220910/https://keepass.info/news/n170109_2.35.html |archive-date=2024-03-14 |access-date=2020-10-11 |website=Keepass}}</ref> However, a separate plugin provides Twofish as an encryption algorithm in KeePass 2.x. In KeePass 1.x (KDB database format), the integrity of the data is checked using a SHA-256 hash of the plaintext, whereas in KeePass 2.x (KDBX database format), the [[Authenticated encryption|authenticity]] of the data is ensured using a HMAC-SHA-256 hash of the ciphertext (Encrypt-then-MAC construction).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reichl |first=Dominik |title=Security |url=https://keepass.info/help/base/security.html#secencrypt |access-date=2020-10-11 |website=KeePass |archive-date=2020-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017135623/https://keepass.info/help/base/security.html#secencrypt |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Notable KeePass derivatives==

* [[KeePassDX]], a fork of KeePass designed for [[Android (operating system)|Android]]
* [[KeePassX]], a multi-platform open source KeePass clone for Linux and macOS, built using the [[Qt (toolkit)|Qt libraries]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Geyer |first=Felix |title=KeePassX 2.0 has arrived |url=https://www.keepassx.org/news/2015/12/533 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222112108/https://www.keepassx.org/news/2015/12/533/ |archive-date=2015-12-22 |access-date=2015-12-07 |publisher=Kee pass X}}</ref> As of December 2021, KeePassX is no longer actively maintained.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 December 2021 |title=Development stopped |url=https://www.keepassx.org/index.html%3Fp=636.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211212092820/https://www.keepassx.org/index.html%3Fp=636.html |archive-date=2021-12-12 |access-date=2021-12-09}}</ref>
* [[KeePassXC]] (KeePass Cross-Platform Community Edition) is a fork of KeePassX written in [[C++]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=KeePassXC Password Manager |url=https://keepassxc.org/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240321090413/https://keepassxc.org/ |archive-date=2024-03-21 |access-date=26 January 2017 |website=KeepassXC}}</ref>
* [[KeeWeb]], a cross-platform [[JavaScript]] web application using the KeePass database format, desktop version built with [[Electron (software framework)|Electron]].
* KyPass, developed by [[Miguel Vanhove]], compatible with Apple platforms<ref>{{Cite web |language=fr |title=KyPass - KeePass in Sync |url=https://apps.apple.com/ch/app/kypass-keepass-in-sync/id1258708743?l=fr |website=App Store |publisher=Apple |access-date=17 May 2026}}</ref> and offering native support for [[Dropbox]], [[OneDrive]] and other online backup services.

== Reception ==
In 2006<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sichere Passwörter - statt Da Vinci Code |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2450857/sichere-passwoerter---statt-da-vinci-code |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=DER STANDARD |language=de-AT}}</ref> and 2016<ref>{{Cite web |title=Schluss mit "123456": 1. Februar ist "Change your password"-Tag |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000030144886/schluss-mit-123456-1-februar-ist-change-your-password-tag |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=DER STANDARD |language=de-AT}}</ref>, [[Der Standard]] highlighted KeePass to its readers as an effective tool for managing and organizing passwords.
